title: Sales and Leases
description: Sales and Leases of Goods under UCC Articles 1, 2 and 2A, Weeks 1–14 (Sepinuck, Chapters 1–7, 9 and 11). Covers which law governs, formation and the battle of the forms, the statute of frauds, warranties and disclaimers, gap fillers, delivery and risk of loss, the parol evidence rule, assignment and delegation, repudiation, excuse, buyer's and seller's remedies, rejection, cure and revocation, privity, and leases under Article 2A.

Sales_and_Leases_Week10_Condensed_Outlin.title: Sales and Leases Outline
Sales_and_Leases_Week10_Condensed_Outlin.description: Condensed outline of Weeks 1–14 for the final exam. 35 sections. Sections I–XVI cover Weeks 1–8: the UCC and governing law, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds and unconscionability, good faith and modification, express and implied warranties, quantity and price, delivery and risk of loss, disclaimers, remedy limits, the parol evidence rule, assignment, termination, insecurity and repudiation, and excuse. Sections XVII–XXXV follow the syllabus through Week 14: buyer's remedies, rejection, cure, acceptance and revocation, privity, seller's remedies, Article 2A leases and finance leases, and final-exam checklists, with every assigned problem worked. Case boxes mark main, note, and cited-only cases with their casebook pages and class slides. Slides on file end at Week 8, so later sections rest on the casebook and statutes.

Sales_and_Leases_Bar_Questions.html.title: Sales and Leases Bar Questions
Sales_and_Leases_Bar_Questions.html.description: 444 bar-style multiple-choice questions on Weeks 1–14: the rules, cases, and assigned problems in the outline, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, buyer's and seller's remedies, privity, and leases under Article 2A. Each question sets out new facts, and every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.

Sales_and_Leases_Practice_Exams.html.title: Sales and Leases Practice Exams
Sales_and_Leases_Practice_Exams.html.description: 58 cumulative practice exams (870 questions) for the final, covering all of Weeks 1–14 and all 35 sections of the course outline, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, buyer's and seller's remedies, privity, and leases under Article 2A. Each exam follows Professor Richardson's sample-exam format: 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions that mix rule questions (“Which of the following is NOT…”) with short hypos asking who wins and why, plus “None of the above” and “All of the above” choices that are sometimes the answer. Every exam samples the whole course, and about 40% of the questions come from the Weeks 8–14 remedies and lease units, including integrated hypos and damages calculations. Every choice has its own explanation. Use Study mode to check answers as you go, or Exam mode to grade a full exam, and pick a topic to drill one outline section by week.

Sales_and_Leases_Statutory_Supplement.ht.title: Sales and Leases Statutory Supplement
Sales_and_Leases_Statutory_Supplement.ht.description: Every UCC section the Weeks 1-14 outline and the practice sets cite (182 sections from Articles 1, 2, 2A, and 9), from Selected Commercial Statutes, 2026 edition, with the Official Comments. Section text is summarized in the statute's own key words and each comment is condensed; comments the outline or the practice questions rely on are marked. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 2-207 to go straight there), filter by any of the outline's first 34 sections, follow cross-references between sections, and open or close all the comments at once.

Sales_and_Leases_Week10_Comprehensive_Ou.description: Full-length source outline for Weeks 1–8, kept off the public site. Use it as the reference when making questions, flowcharts, and flashcards for this subject.
PDF copy of the comprehensive outline, kept off the public site.

Sales_and_Leases_Playlist.title: Sales and Leases Playlist
Sales_and_Leases_Playlist.description: Sixteen study songs that cover all 16 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, repudiation, and excuse. The main cases are sung through: Daitom, Casazza, Market Street, Roth Steel, Rogath, Orange & Rockland, Mathis, Razor, Santa Fe, Top of Iowa, and NIPSCO. It starts with track 1 and plays straight through; pick any track from the list, at 0.5×, 0.75×, normal, 1.25×, or 1.5× speed.

1_Is_It_Goods.mp3.title: Is It Goods?
1_Is_It_Goods.mp3.topic: Outline §1 · Scope and which law governs
1_Is_It_Goods.mp3.description: The four factors that pick the governing law, what counts as goods under § 2-105 (and what does not: money, securities, things in action), things attached to land under § 2-107, and mixed deals of goods and services: the predominant-purpose test, the gravamen test from Anthony Pools, and the 2022 two-tier rule for hybrid transactions.

2_Battle_of_the_Forms.mp3.title: Battle of the Forms
2_Battle_of_the_Forms.mp3.description: A duet between buyer and seller. Formation under §§ 2-204 and 2-206, merchants' firm offers under § 2-205, and § 2-207: an acceptance with different terms still accepts unless it is expressly conditional, additional terms between merchants, and the knock-out rule. Case: Daitom v. Pennwalt, where the clashing limitation clauses dropped out and the four-year period of § 2-725 filled the gap.

3_You_Never_Signed_It.mp3.title: You Never Signed It
3_You_Never_Signed_It.mp3.topic: Outline §3 · Statute of frauds and unconscionability
3_You_Never_Signed_It.mp3.description: The § 2-201 writing rule for sales of $500 or more (a record, signed by the party sued, stating a quantity), the four exceptions, and why promissory estoppel did not save the buyer in Casazza v. Kiser. Then § 2-302 unconscionability: procedural and substantive, decided by the court as of the time the deal was made.

4_Good_Faith.mp3.title: Good Faith
4_Good_Faith.mp3.topic: Outline §4 · Good faith and course of performance
4_Good_Faith.mp3.description: The § 1-304 duty of good faith (honesty in fact plus fair dealing), which cannot be disclaimed and is not a claim of its own. Market Street Associates v. Frey on exploiting the other side's oversight, with Brunswick Hills and Vintage Rodeo, and the § 1-303 hierarchy: express terms, course of performance, course of dealing, usage of trade.

5_Pay_More_or_Get_Nothing.mp3.title: Pay More or Get Nothing
5_Pay_More_or_Get_Nothing.mp3.description: Section 2-209: modifications need no consideration but must be in good faith, and Roth Steel v. Sharon Steel holds that a price increase extracted by threatening to stop performing is not. No-oral-modification clauses, the statute of frauds applied to the deal as modified, waiver and its retraction, and estoppel.

6_Promise_or_Puff.mp3.title: Promise or Puff?
6_Promise_or_Puff.mp3.description: The three ways to make an express warranty under § 2-313 (affirmation of fact, description, sample or model), the basis-of-the-bargain test without proof of reliance, and the line between specific facts and puffing. Case: Rogath v. Siebenmann, the Francis Bacon painting, on whether a buyer who learns of doubts still keeps the warranty.

7_Implied.mp3.title: Implied
7_Implied.mp3.description: Merchantability under § 2-314 and its six standards, fitness for a particular purpose under § 2-315 (with the Ingram River barges), and the warranty of title and against infringement under § 2-312. Also voidable title and entrustment under § 2-403, and the three privity alternatives of § 2-318.

8_Fill_in_the_Blanks.mp3.title: Fill in the Blanks
8_Fill_in_the_Blanks.mp3.topic: Outline §6–7 · Gap fillers, quantity and price
8_Fill_in_the_Blanks.mp3.description: Open terms under § 2-204(3) and the delivery, time, and payment gap fillers. Output and requirements contracts under § 2-306 (good faith and no unreasonably disproportionate quantity, from Orange & Rockland v. Amerada Hess), and open price under § 2-305, including a price set by one party in bad faith in Mathis v. Exxon and the majority view that rejects it.

9_Accept_or_Reject.mp3.title: Accept or Reject
9_Accept_or_Reject.mp3.description: Tender and payment as concurrent conditions, the seller's tender under § 2-503, the buyer's right to inspect under § 2-513, acceptance under § 2-606, perfect tender and installment contracts, cure under § 2-508, the buyer's duties after rejecting, and revocation of acceptance under § 2-608.

10_Risk_of_Loss.mp3.title: Risk of Loss
10_Risk_of_Loss.mp3.description: A call-and-response duet on who bears the loss when goods are destroyed. The agreement first, then the breaching party under § 2-510, then § 2-509: shipment and destination contracts, goods held by a bailee, and everything else (merchant sellers on receipt, non-merchants on tender). Also F.O.B. and C.I.F. terms and the seller's shipping duties under § 2-504.

11_Make_It_Conspicuous.mp3.title: Make It Conspicuous
11_Make_It_Conspicuous.mp3.topic: Outline §10 · Variation by agreement and disclaimers
11_Make_It_Conspicuous.mp3.description: What § 1-302 lets the parties change and what it does not, and disclaimers under § 2-316: mention merchantability, put fitness in a conspicuous writing, "as is" and "with all faults," examination of the goods, and trade usage. Why express warranties are nearly impossible to disclaim, and why title needs specific language.

12_Two_Walls.mp3.title: Two Walls
12_Two_Walls.mp3.description: The buyer's and seller's damage formulas, incidental and consequential damages under § 2-715, liquidated damages under § 2-718, and limited remedies under § 2-719. Case: Razor v. Hyundai, where the repair remedy failed of its essential purpose but the exclusion of consequential damages stood or fell on its own, as unconscionable.

13_Parol_Evidence_Rule.mp3.title: Parol Evidence Rule
13_Parol_Evidence_Rule.mp3.description: Section 2-202: a final writing cannot be contradicted by prior or contemporaneous agreements but can be explained or supplemented, and a complete and exclusive one cannot be supplemented either. What the rule never bars (later modifications, fraud, conditions precedent), how merger clauses work, and how it interacts with § 2-316(1) when oral warranties meet an "as is" writing.

14_Passing_It_On.mp3.title: Passing It On
14_Passing_It_On.mp3.description: Assigning rights and delegating duties under § 2-210, anti-assignment clauses and § 9-406(d), and the difference between cancellation and termination under § 2-106. Then ending an indefinite contract on reasonable notice under § 2-309, with Santa Fe Custom Shutters v. Home Depot: no lost profits for ending an at-will deal.

15_Adequate_Assurance.mp3.title: Adequate Assurance
15_Adequate_Assurance.mp3.description: A duet between an anxious party and a reassuring one. Demanding adequate assurance under § 2-609 and the 30-day limit, anticipatory repudiation under § 2-610, and retraction under § 2-611. Cases: Top of Iowa Coop v. Sime Farms on hedge-to-arrive corn contracts, and PDM v. Brookhaven on demanding more than is adequate.

16_Excuse.mp3.title: Excuse
16_Excuse.mp3.description: The closing anthem. Casualty to identified goods under § 2-613, substituted performance under § 2-614, impracticability and fair allocation under §§ 2-615 and 2-616, and frustration of purpose at common law. Case: NIPSCO v. Carbon County Coal, where a buyer that misjudged the market could not walk away from a fixed-price contract.
